title: Your own story
job: An eight-sentence account, built from the whole ladder
verifiedBy: Claude Opus 5 — LLM review, authorised by repo owner

rules.text: EACH ITEM IS AN ACCOUNT OF AT MOST EIGHT SENTENCES, and the word bound applies to each sentence inside it rather than to the whole. Eight is a ceiling and not a target: a five-sentence story that holds together beats an eight-sentence one padded to the number.

THE SPEAKER IS NAMED ONCE. jeo-neun opens the account and then disappears; four sentences that each begin with it read as insistent, or as a list of unrelated facts. This is L2-M10's zero anaphora stretched from four sentences to eight.

A NEW PARTICIPANT ARRIVES WITH -i/-ga AND COMES BACK WITH -eun/-neun. chingu-ga … then chingu-neun …. Marking every return with -i/-ga reads as though each mention were a different friend, which is L3-M1's law running across a whole paragraph rather than a pair.

THE ENDING ENVELOPE, named so an author can stay inside it: L1-M5's past, L1-M4's present, L1-M6's -l geoyeyo, L2-M7's -go isseoyo, L2-M8's an and mot, L3-M2's modifiers, L3-M4's -(eu)myeon, L3-M5's -dago, L3-M6's -gess- and -a/eo haeyo, and L3-M9's -deon with its one double past.

WHAT STAYS OUT: the past counterfactual (L4-M3), every time clause including -(eu)l ttae (L4-M6), -(seu)pnida and -(eu)psida (L4-M7), the past-habit system (L4-M8), the passive, and banmal as a written sentence anywhere at all.

REGISTER IS CHOSEN BY THE LISTENER AND HELD FOR THE WHOLE ACCOUNT — and in this course the choice is between TWO values, not three. S05 and S06 are one story told twice: the elder version puts -kkeseo on its subject and the honorific on its verb, the friend version stays plain -yo, and neither is banmal.

A STORY HAS A SHAPE AND NOT JUST A SEQUENCE: something wanted, something in the way, how it ended. What turns a timetable into an account is a REASON (L1-M9's -aseo, or geuraeseo), a FEELING (L3-M6's), and one REPORTED line (L3-M5's -dago), which is what puts other people in it.

THE PAST OF A FEELING LANDS HERE, exactly as L3-M6 said it would. apasseoyo, joasseoyo, seulpeosseoyo, buranhaesseoyo, himdeureosseoyo are L1-M5's -eoss- on words that module kept in the present; no ending is opened, only shapes of what the ladder already owns.

sentences.display: Jeo-neun eoje hoesa-eseo ilhaesseoyo. Meori-ga apasseoyo. Geuraeseo ilchik jip-e gasseoyo. Yak-eul meogeosseoyo. Jigeum-eun gwaenchanayo.
sentences.script: 저는 어제 회사에서 일했어요. 머리가 아팠어요. 그래서 일찍 집에 갔어요. 약을 먹었어요. 지금은 괜찮아요.
sentences.cue: I worked at the office yesterday. I had a headache, so I went home early. I took some medicine. I'm fine now.
sentences.literal: I-topic yesterday company-at worked. head-subject hurt. so early house-to went. medicine-object ate. now-topic is-fine

words.note: L2-M8's apayo with L1-M5's past on it. L3-M7 kept every ache in the present; the day it happened on is what puts it here.

sentences.trap: jeo-neun APPEARS ONCE AND NEVER RETURNS. Every later sentence has no subject at all, and the account still says who throughout — putting jeo-neun back in front of Meori-ga apasseoyo would sound like a correction of somebody else's headache.
sentences.sound: The five sentences run down in pitch and each ends flat; only Jigeum-eun lifts, because it is the turn from then to now.

variations.changed: L2-M5's bae in the second sentence, and nothing else moves

variations.cue: So I went to the hospital.
variations.changed: a different consequence off the same reason word

mistake.display: Jeo-neun meori-ga apasseoyo. Jeo-neun jip-e gasseoyo.
mistake.script: 저는 머리가 아팠어요. 저는 집에 갔어요.
mistake.why: Naming yourself in every sentence breaks the account into unrelated facts. Say jeo-neun once, at the start.

sentences.usage: Explaining an absence, the morning after.

sentences.display: Jeo-neun eoje chingu-reul mannasseoyo. Chingu-ga hoesa-eseo ilhaeyo. Chingu-neun jeongmal bappayo. Gachi keopi-reul masyeosseoyo. Jeongmal joasseoyo.
sentences.script: 저는 어제 친구를 만났어요. 친구가 회사에서 일해요. 친구는 정말 바빠요. 같이 커피를 마셨어요. 정말 좋았어요.
sentences.cue: I met a friend yesterday. She works at a company and she's really busy. We had coffee together. It was lovely.
sentences.literal: I-topic yesterday friend-object met. friend-subject company-at works. friend-topic really is-busy. together coffee-object drank. really was-good

words.note: L1-M9's joayo in the past. It closes an account the way English lovely does, and it says how the whole thing felt rather than how one moment did.

sentences.trap: chingu-ga THEN chingu-neun, AND THE ORDER MATTERS. The first mention introduces her and the second one returns to her; swapping them makes the second friend read as a different person.
sentences.sound: chingu-ga and chingu-neun are the two beats the account turns on — the first slightly stressed, the second flat.

variations.cue: My friend works at a company.
variations.changed: the return particle used at the first mention, which is what makes it wrong in the account
L1-M3's bibimbap where the coffee was

mistake.display: Jeo-neun chingu-reul mannasseoyo. Chingu-ga bappayo. Chingu-ga keopi-reul masyeosseoyo.
mistake.script: 저는 친구를 만났어요. 친구가 바빠요. 친구가 커피를 마셨어요.
mistake.why: Three -ga marks read as three different friends. The second and third mentions take -neun, or no particle at all.

sentences.usage: Telling somebody how you spent an afternoon.

sentences.display: Eoje siheom-eul bwasseoyo. Jeo-neun jom buranhaesseoyo. Hajiman chingu-ga gwaenchantago haesseoyo. Geuraeseo gibun-i joasseoyo.
sentences.script: 어제 시험을 봤어요. 저는 좀 불안했어요. 하지만 친구가 괜찮다고 했어요. 그래서 기분이 좋았어요.
sentences.cue: I sat an exam yesterday. I was a bit anxious, but a friend told me it was fine, so I felt better.
sentences.literal: yesterday exam-object saw. I-topic a-bit was-anxious. but friend-subject fine-that said. so mood-subject was-good

words.note: L2-M1's gwaenchanayo inside L3-M5's report frame. What was said keeps its own plain shape and -dago carries it to haesseoyo.
L3-M6's buranhaeyo in the past. The feeling belongs to the exam that is now over, which is exactly what the past ending says.

sentences.trap: THE REPORTED CLAUSE DOES NOT BECOME POLITE. gwaenchanayo-go is not Korean; the -yo is stripped and the plain gwaenchanta is what -dago attaches to, however polite the sentence around it is.
sentences.sound: gwaenchantago is four syllables with the stress even across them; the -dago runs straight into haesseoyo.

variations.cue: A friend said it was fine.
variations.changed: the reported line on its own, out of the account
the present, which moves the good mood from that day to this one

mistake.why: The -yo is dropped before -dago: Chingu-ga gwaenchantago haesseoyo.

sentences.usage: An account with somebody else's words inside it.

sentences.display: Yejeon-e-neun Seollal-e halmeoni-ga tteokguk-eul mandeureosseoyo. Halmeoni-ga mandeuldeon tteokguk-i jeongmal masisseoyo. Jigeum-eun je-ga mandeureoyo. Hajiman dallayo. Jom seulpeosseoyo.
sentences.script: 예전에는 설날에 할머니가 떡국을 만들었어요. 할머니가 만들던 떡국이 정말 맛있어요. 지금은 제가 만들어요. 하지만 달라요. 좀 슬펐어요.
sentences.cue: My grandmother used to make tteokguk at Seollal. The tteokguk she used to make was really good. I make it now, but it's different. It made me a little sad.
sentences.literal: before-topic Seollal-on grandmother-subject rice-soup-object made. grandmother-subject used-to-make rice-soup-subject really is-delicious. now-topic I-subject make. but is-different. a-bit was-sad

words.cue: was sad · it made me sad
words.note: L3-M6's seulpeoyo in the past. Of yourself it stays the descriptive verb; only somebody else's sadness would need the -a/eo haeyo shape.

sentences.trap: -deon AND THE PLAIN PAST DO DIFFERENT WORK IN THE SAME PARAGRAPH. mandeureosseoyo says she made it; mandeuldeon tteokguk says the tteokguk she used to make, and only the second is looking back at a habit.
sentences.sound: The account slows at mandeuldeon — the -deon is held, and it is what tells a listener a memory is coming.

variations.cue: The songpyeon she used to make is delicious.
variations.changed: L3-M9's other festival food under the same remembered clause
the turn from then to now, standing on its own

mistake.why: jeo becomes je in front of -ga, as L3-M2 taught: Jigeum-eun je-ga mandeureoyo.

sentences.usage: A memory told at a family table, or to somebody who asks about the food.

sentences.display: Eoje seonsaengnim-i hoeui-e wasseoyo. Seonsaengnim-eun jeongmal chinjeolhaeyo. Jeo-neun jom buranhaesseoyo. Hajiman seonsaengnim-i dowajwosseoyo. Jeongmal gomawoyo.
sentences.script: 어제 선생님이 회의에 왔어요. 선생님은 정말 친절해요. 저는 좀 불안했어요. 하지만 선생님이 도와줬어요. 정말 고마워요.
sentences.cue: The teacher came to the meeting yesterday. She's really kind. I was a bit anxious, but she helped me. I'm really grateful.
sentences.literal: yesterday teacher-subject meeting-to came. teacher-topic really is-kind. I-topic a-bit was-anxious. but teacher-subject helped. really am-grateful

words.note: L2-M1's dowajuseyo as a plain past statement. The -jwo- is the same give that makes every -a/eo juseyo request, reporting a kindness rather than asking for one.

sentences.trap: THIS IS THE SAME STORY AS S06 AND THE REGISTER IS THE ONLY DIFFERENCE. Told to a friend, the teacher takes plain -i and the verbs stay bare; nothing here is banmal, and nothing here is honorific.
sentences.sound: Even and unhurried; seonsaengnim-i and seonsaengnim-eun are the two beats, exactly as chingu-ga and chingu-neun were in S02.

variations.changed: the kindness on its own, out of the account
a participant nobody would honour, which is why the plain form is right

mistake.why: Two faults: je-ga, not jeo-ga, and the honorific can never sit on your own verb. Je-ga seonsaengnim-eul dowajwosseoyo.

sentences.usage: Telling a friend about somebody who was good to you.

sentences.display: Eoje seonsaengnim-kkeseo hoeui-e osyeosseoyo. Seonsaengnim-eun jeongmal chinjeolhaeyo. Jeo-neun jom buranhaesseoyo. Hajiman seonsaengnim-kkeseo dowajusyeosseoyo. Jeongmal gamsahamnida.
sentences.script: 어제 선생님께서 회의에 오셨어요. 선생님은 정말 친절해요. 저는 좀 불안했어요. 하지만 선생님께서 도와주셨어요. 정말 감사합니다.
sentences.cue: The teacher came to the meeting yesterday. She is very kind. I was a bit anxious, but she helped me. I'm very grateful.
sentences.literal: yesterday teacher-honorific-subject meeting-to came-honorific. teacher-topic really is-kind. I-topic a-bit was-anxious. but teacher-honorific-subject helped-honorific. really thank-you

words.note: S05's dowajwosseoyo with L3-M8's -si- inside it. The helper is raised, never the speaker, and the same -syeoss- makes osyeosseoyo.

sentences.trap: THE HONORIFIC MOVES, THE SPEECH LEVEL DOES NOT. Both tellings are -yo sentences; what changes is -i to -kkeseo and the -si- inside the verb. The clerk's -(seu)pnida is still not written, and gamsahamnida is one of the four frozen phrases the course already owns.
sentences.sound: -kkeseo is a small held beat before the verb, and osyeosseoyo carries its stress on the SYEO.

variations.changed: the raised sentence on its own, beside S05's plain one

variations.cue: The teacher came to the meeting.
variations.changed: the opening line alone, with both halves of the honorific visible

mistake.why: Never of yourself. Of your own arrival it is Jeo-neun hoeui-e wasseoyo.

sentences.usage: The same account, told to somebody senior to both of you.

sentences.display: Naeil-eun je saengil-ieyo. Chingu-deul-i jip-e wayo. Jeo-neun tteokguk-eul mandeul geoyeyo. Jeongmal sinnayo.
sentences.script: 내일은 제 생일이에요. 친구들이 집에 와요. 저는 떡국을 만들 거예요. 정말 신나요.
sentences.cue: Tomorrow is my birthday. My friends are coming over. I'm going to make tteokguk. I'm really excited.
sentences.literal: tomorrow-topic my birthday-is. friend-plural-subject house-to come. I-topic rice-soup-object will make. really am-excited

words.note: L3-M8's mandeureoyo in L1-M6's -l geoyeyo frame. The l of the stem is already there, so nothing is added in front of geoyeyo.

sentences.trap: sinnayo IS ABOUT NOW EVEN IN A PLAN. The excitement is the state you are in today; the party itself is what -l geoyeyo covers, and mixing them gives a sentence that is excited about being excited.
sentences.sound: mandeul geoyeyo is two words with a clean break; the l is held before the g.

variations.changed: the plain present used for a settled arrangement, as L1-M4 taught
L3-M9's other festival food in the plan

mistake.why: The stem already ends in l, so no -eu- is added: Jeo-neun tteokguk-eul mandeul geoyeyo.

sentences.usage: Telling somebody what is happening tomorrow, and how you feel about it.
sentences.mnemonic: The plan is future, the feeling is now.

sentences.display: Jeo-neun eoje eunhaeng-e gasseoyo. Meonjeo sincheongseo-reul sseosseoyo. Geu daeum-e gyejwa-reul mandeureosseoyo. Machimnae kadeu-reul badasseoyo. Jom himdeureosseoyo.
sentences.script: 저는 어제 은행에 갔어요. 먼저 신청서를 썼어요. 그 다음에 계좌를 만들었어요. 마침내 카드를 받았어요. 좀 힘들었어요.
sentences.cue: I went to the bank yesterday. First I filled in the form, then I opened an account, and finally I got the card. It was a bit of a slog.
sentences.literal: I-topic yesterday bank-to went. first application-form-object wrote. that next-at account-object made. finally card-object received. a-bit was-hard

words.note: The plain past of the verb inside L2-M1's sseojuseyo. The request form asks somebody to do it; this reports that you did.
L2-M3's badayo in the past. L3-M8's badeuseyo tells somebody to take a thing; this says the thing reached you.

sentences.trap: L2-M10's THREE SEQUENCING WORDS CARRY THE WHOLE STRUCTURE. meonjeo, geu daeum-e and machimnae are all this account needs to be ordered, and no time clause is written anywhere — those belong to L4-M6.
sentences.sound: The three sequencing words each take a small lift, and the last sentence drops away flat.

variations.cue: First I filled in the form.
variations.changed: the first step alone, as an answer to what did you do

variations.cue: I finally got my ID card.
variations.changed: L3-M8's other document at the end of the same errand

mistake.display: Meonjeo sincheongseo-reul sseosseoyo. Meonjeo gyejwa-reul mandeureosseoyo.
mistake.script: 먼저 신청서를 썼어요. 먼저 계좌를 만들었어요.
mistake.why: Only one step can be first. The second is geu daeum-e and the last is machimnae.

sentences.usage: Reporting an errand that took longer than it should have.

sentences.display: Oneul-eun Chuseok-ieyo. Saram-deul-i hanbok-eul ipgo isseoyo. Jeo-neun songpyeon-eul meogeosseoyo. Jeongmal masisseoyo. Gibun-i joayo.
sentences.script: 오늘은 추석이에요. 사람들이 한복을 입고 있어요. 저는 송편을 먹었어요. 정말 맛있어요. 기분이 좋아요.
sentences.cue: Today is Chuseok. People are wearing hanbok. I ate songpyeon — it's really good. I'm in a good mood.
sentences.literal: today-topic Chuseok-is. person-plural-subject hanbok-object wear-and are. I-topic songpyeon-object ate. really is-delicious. mood-subject is-good

words.note: With isseoyo it is the state of having clothes on, not the act of dressing — the one verb class where -go isseoyo reads as a state. L3-M9's ipeun saram says the same thing with a clause.

sentences.trap: ipgo isseoyo AND ipeun saram MEAN THE SAME THING. English has one wearing for both; Korean offers the progressive and L3-M2's past modifier, and neither is more correct than the other here.
sentences.sound: ipgo isseoyo is said as one run, IP-go-i-sseo-yo, with the p unreleased.

variations.cue: There are a lot of people wearing hanbok.
variations.changed: L3-M9's clause saying the same thing with no progressive in it
the wrong festival food, and the sentence still works — it is the day that decides

mistake.why: One person, in a sentence about a crowd. Saram-deul-i hanbok-eul ipgo isseoyo.

sentences.usage: A message sent from the middle of a holiday.

sentences.display: Meonjeo hangungmal-eul baewosseoyo. Jeongmal himdeureosseoyo. Hajiman chingu-ga gwaenchantago haesseoyo. Geu daeum-e maeil gongbuhaesseoyo. Machimnae siheom-eul bwasseoyo. Jigeum-eun hangungmal-eul jaju haeyo. Jeongmal gippeoyo.
sentences.script: 먼저 한국말을 배웠어요. 정말 힘들었어요. 하지만 친구가 괜찮다고 했어요. 그 다음에 매일 공부했어요. 마침내 시험을 봤어요. 지금은 한국말을 자주 해요. 정말 기뻐요.
sentences.cue: First I learned some Korean. It was really hard, but a friend told me it was fine. Then I studied every day, and finally I sat the exam. I speak Korean often now. I'm really glad.
sentences.literal: first Korean-object learned. really was-hard. but friend-subject fine-that said. that next-at every-day studied. finally exam-object saw. now-topic Korean-object often do. really am-glad

words.note: L1-M9's baewoyo in the past. It is the whole ladder's own verb, and this account is the first place a learner uses it about themselves.
L3-M6's himdeureoyo in the past. It is the something-in-the-way of this story, and without it the account is a timetable.

sentences.trap: SEVEN SENTENCES AND ONE NAMED SUBJECT. jeo-neun does not appear at all here: the first clause carries no topic and the account still reads as yours from beginning to end, which is what L2-M10 was building towards.
sentences.sound: The three sequencing words mark the shape; jigeum-eun lifts, and the last sentence is said slowly.

variations.changed: the turn to now, standing on its own as an answer

variations.cue: I couldn't speak Korean well before.
variations.changed: L2-M8's mot and L3-M9's yejeon-e-neun opening the same story from the other end

mistake.display: Meonjeo hangungmal-eul baewosseoyo. Geu daeum-e hangungmal-eul baewosseoyo.
mistake.script: 먼저 한국말을 배웠어요. 그 다음에 한국말을 배웠어요.
mistake.why: A sequence needs different steps, not the same one twice. An account with no obstacle in it is a timetable.

sentences.usage: The story a learner is asked for most often, and the one this course exists to hand over.
